title: FACET — one stone, one orbit, one spectrum
vector: The camera only ever advances along one slow clockwise orbit, drawing closer to the stone — never reversing, never cutting.

keyframes.prompt: Ultra-dark circular museum chamber of black stone, near-black palette, deep ink shadow. At the exact center, a rough uncut black crystal stone rests on a low basalt plinth. One thin hairline of white light rests on the stone's shoulder, casting a faint cold rim along one edge; a few fine dust motes hang in the beam. Everything else falls to darkness. High-end cinematic product-film still, restrained, minimal, dozens of details never hundreds, no text, no people, no logos.

Same ink-dark circular chamber, same rough black stone on the basalt plinth, same hairline beam, but the camera has orbited about thirty degrees clockwise and the stone now shows ONE clean sheared plane cut into its rough surface, the new facet catching a cold cyan-white rim light. The rest of the stone stays rough and black. Deep shadow everywhere else, restrained, no text, no people.

Same chamber, same stone, camera orbited further clockwise. The stone now shows THREE clean cut facets among the rough black surface, each facet holding its own restrained rim hue — one cold cyan, one violet, one a whisper of amber. Thin dust motes in the hairline beam. Everything else deep ink darkness, dozens of details never hundreds, no text, no people.

Same chamber, camera near profile view of the stone. Most of the rough surface is now cut away: the stone has become a dark crystalline polyhedron with sharp clean facets, and deep inside its heart a compressed white glow has ignited, like captured starlight. Rim hues deepen to violet and magenta. The first very faint colored reflections touch the dark floor beneath the plinth. Restrained, museum-dark, no text, no people.

Same chamber, camera past profile orbiting toward the far side. The prism is now fully cut and complete: every facet sharp and clean, the compressed white core glowing steady inside the dark crystal. One thin spectral gleam begins along the base where the prism meets the plinth — a hair of separated color, cyan and violet. Chamber stays deep ink, minimal, no text, no people.

Same ink-dark chamber, camera completing the orbit to the front of the finished prism. The dark cut prism holds its compressed white core and exhales ONE restrained spectrum fan: thin separated rays of cyan, violet, magenta and amber stretching low across the dark stone floor like light through a prism, elegant and few. The world reference is a dark jewel prism resting on black rocks with spectral light — match that grade: deep blacks, opulent shadow, spectrum only on rims and rays, never fills, never rainbow. Everything else deep ink. Final, still, silent, no text, no people.
